conclusion.justification: The report concludes that the scientific consensus, based on large RCTs and comprehensive meta-analyses, shows ivermectin does not meaningfully lower COVID-19 mortality, clearly rejecting the claim.
conclusion.label: rejects

report:
The evidence does not support the claim that ivermectin lowers COVID-19 mortality — current best evidence points the other way.

Early, smaller studies (some later retracted or of poor quality) suggested benefit, and low-quality meta-analyses reported reduced mortality with "low certainty of evidence" (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S187140212100206X). However, these were superseded by large, rigorous randomized controlled trials. The TOGETHER trial, a major multi-center RCT published in NEJM, found no significant reduction in hospitalization or clinical worsening with ivermectin compared to placebo (14.7% vs. 16.3%), and follow-up correspondence in NEJM confirmed no meaningful benefit (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMc2207995). ACTIV-6, another large RCT, similarly found ivermectin was not effective as a COVID-19 treatment (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivermectin_during_the_COVID-19_pandemic).

The most recent and comprehensive systematic review and meta-analysis (33 RCTs, n=10,489, through June 2023) concluded that ivermectin did not reduce the risk of mortality in COVID-19 patients (https://www.cell.com/heliyon/fulltext/S2405-8440(24)03678-8). Other meta-analyses similarly found ivermectin did not significantly improve mortality, ICU admission, or ventilator use, though it may modestly reduce symptoms. The World Health Organization currently recommends ivermectin only within clinical trials, citing "very low certainty" evidence for mortality benefit.

**Conclusion:** The scientific consensus, based on large RCTs and the most rigorous recent meta-analyses, is that ivermectin does **not** meaningfully lower COVID-19 mortality. Early positive findings were driven by smaller, lower-quality, or flawed studies; as evidence quality improved, the apparent benefit disappeared.
